sources.title: Best available techniques: environmental permits
facts: Environment Agency and Defra guidance updated 8 January 2026.
BAT and BAT-associated emission levels are permit-setting standards; derogations require justification.
A BAT requirement or AEL is not a measured emission result.

sources.title: UK BAT group
facts: Official UK BAT programme page lists sector BATC status and draft reports.
Drafting, consultation and implementation status must be preserved.
BATC status is regulatory evidence, not physical emissions observation.

sources.title: Industrial emissions standards and best available techniques
facts: Defra guidance explains IED and BAT controls for larger industrial facilities.
BAT addresses emissions to air, water and land.
Industrial standards do not by themselves quantify facility or parcel emissions.

sources.title: Industrial emissions proposed UK BAT consultation
facts: Published 19 March 2026.
Consultation covers ferrous forming, galvanising, textiles and common waste-gas treatment in chemicals.
Consultation proposals are not final BATC or observed emissions.

sources.title: Defra UK BAT consultation portal
facts: Official Defra consultation closed 14 May 2026.
Draft BAT-AELs and BAT-AEPLs were consulted on before finalisation.
Consultation evidence must not be promoted to final permit limits or measured emissions.

sources.title: Establishing UK BAT policy paper
facts: Official policy paper on establishment of the UK BAT regime.
UK BAT is an evidence-led standard-setting mechanism.
Policy framework is not an emissions dataset.

sources.title: Establishing UK BAT accessible policy
facts: Describes BAT techniques, BATC and implementation framework.
Existing EU BATC continue where retained; new UK BATC are developed through UK process.
Standards and techniques remain distinct from monitoring results.

sources.title: Energy efficiency standards for industrial permits
facts: Environment Agency guidance requires energy-efficiency measures for relevant industrial permits.
Energy management, CCA and BAT pathways affect permit evidence.
Energy-efficiency compliance or opportunity identification is not a direct GHG observation.

sources.title: Technical guidance for regulated industry sectors
facts: Environment Agency collection updated 8 July 2026.
Collection links sector guidance for combustion, waste, chemicals, hydrogen and other regulated activities.
Catalogue membership and sector scope do not establish measured emissions.

sources.title: Air emissions risk assessment for environmental permits
facts: Risk assessment compares process contribution and predicted environmental concentration with environmental standards.
PC and PEC can involve screening and detailed modelling.
Modelled ambient impact is not a direct stack or parcel emission measurement.

sources.title: Emergency backup diesel engines BAT
facts: Environment Agency BAT guidance for emergency diesel engines on IED installations.
Guidance focuses on NOx control and operating conditions.
BAT design or guidance-level concentrations are not annual GHG mass measurements.

sources.title: Hydrogen combustion emission limit values
facts: Regulator guidance sets ELVs for hydrogen combustion plant above 1 MWth.
Hydrogen combustion has no direct CO2 from the hydrogen fuel but can emit NOx and CO.
Fuel choice or ELV compliance must not be treated as zero lifecycle or parcel GHG.

sources.title: Post-combustion CO2 capture emerging techniques
facts: Environment Agency guidance covers post-combustion carbon capture for power and energy-from-waste plants.
Monitoring may include CO2 mass balance, capture rate and CO2 released.
Captured, stored, used and emitted CO2 require separate accounting boundaries.

sources.title: Hydrogen production with carbon capture emerging techniques
facts: Guidance covers industrial hydrogen production from methane or refinery fuel gas with carbon capture.
Captured CO2 may be transported for permanent geological storage.
Plant design, capture rate and downstream storage are distinct evidence stages.

sources.title: Hydrogen electrolysis emerging techniques
facts: Official regulator guidance covers industrial hydrogen production by water electrolysis.
It addresses energy, water, emissions, monitoring and fugitive hydrogen risks.
Electrolyser production or electricity use is not direct parcel GHG without compatible activity and factor evidence.

sources.title: Hydrogen gasification and pyrolysis emerging-techniques review
facts: Environment Agency evidence review published 17 December 2025.
The review supports future guidance and is explicitly not final guidance.
Technology review evidence is not observed emissions data.

sources.title: Hydrogen methane with carbon capture evidence review
facts: Official evidence review supports regulator emerging-techniques guidance.
It discusses environmental issues and performance evidence for hydrogen with CO2 capture.
Evidence-review performance assumptions must not be promoted to actual site measurements.

sources.title: Hydrogen electrolysis evidence review
facts: Official evidence review for water-electrolysis technologies.
It informs guidance and future BAT development.
Evidence review and future BAT are distinct from site monitoring results.

sources.title: Waste batteries appropriate measures
facts: Environment Agency manual published 21 May 2026.
It covers management, treatment, emissions control, monitoring and process efficiency for permitted battery facilities.
Permit guidance is not a facility emissions dataset.

sources.title: Waste batteries appropriate-measures applicability
facts: Defines when BAT or necessary appropriate measures apply to battery facilities.
Applicability depends on activity, size, nature and site location.
Applicable standard does not imply measured emissions or parcel attribution.

sources.title: Waste batteries general management
facts: Requires an environmental management system and performance procedures.
Objectives and targets are management controls.
Management targets are not observed physical emissions.

sources.title: Waste batteries pre-acceptance and tracking
facts: Sets risk-based waste pre-acceptance, acceptance and tracking controls.
Battery chemistry and waste tracking are activity data.
Waste receipt or chemistry does not directly quantify GHG emissions.

sources.title: Waste batteries storage and handling
facts: Sets pollution-prevention measures for storage and handling.
Handling controls and storage design reduce risk but are not emission observations.
Waste inventory and site location remain distinct from parcel GHG measurement.

sources.title: Waste batteries treatment measures
facts: Sets appropriate measures for battery sorting, preparation and treatment.
Treatment technology or throughput is not direct atmospheric GHG measurement.
Process steps must remain distinct from release measurements.

sources.title: Waste batteries emissions control
facts: Requires identification, characterisation and control of point and diffuse emissions.
Abatement systems and stack/vent design are control evidence.
Control equipment presence is not an observed emissions mass.

sources.title: Waste batteries emissions monitoring and limits
facts: Defines emissions inventories, monitoring methods, frequencies and limits for relevant air and water pollutants.
Point-source records include flow, concentration and load characteristics.
ELVs and scheduled monitoring must not be confused with actual GHG mass or parcel binding.

sources.title: Waste batteries process efficiency
facts: Requires annual review of water, energy, raw materials, residues and wastewater.
Specific energy consumption may be expressed per tonne processed.
Energy intensity or resource use is not absolute GHG without compatible conversion evidence.

sources.title: Waste batteries proposed guidance consultation outcome
facts: Consultation outcome updated 21 May 2026 after final guidance publication.
Original proposed guidance was consulted on before finalisation.
Proposal and final guidance vintages must not be conflated.

sources.title: Waste batteries consultation response
facts: Official response summarises consultation feedback and actions.
Responses support finalisation of emissions-control and monitoring guidance.
Stakeholder response counts are not emissions measurements.

sources.title: Crematoria process guidance note
facts: Statutory process guidance updated 7 July 2026.
Local-authority regulators use it to assess applications and write permits.
Permit guidance and standards do not by themselves quantify emissions.

sources.title: Crematoria technical guidance scope
facts: Updated 7 July 2026 and defines regulated cremator types and scope.
The guidance excludes activities outside regulated human cremation.
Activity scope is not a measured pollutant or GHG quantity.

sources.title: Crematoria process fuels and flue-gas treatment
facts: Describes cremator types, fuels, treatment and operating distinctions.
Temporary and small-scale cremators have different monitoring or permitting conditions.
Exemption or reduced monitoring does not mean zero emissions.

sources.title: Crematoria emissions limits and monitoring
facts: Updated 7 July 2026 and includes operational controls, monitoring and emission limits.
Compliance uses specified reference conditions and repeated measurements.
ELV compliance data must not be promoted to annual parcel GHG without compatible mass and geometry evidence.

sources.title: Crematoria best available techniques
facts: Updated 7 July 2026.
BAT covers combustion control, flue-gas treatment, energy recovery and management.
BAT technique or target is not a measurement result.

sources.title: Crematoria national emergency standards
facts: Updated 3 June 2026 and covers emergency planning and permit breaches.
Emergency operating provisions are conditional regulatory evidence.
Emergency status does not create or quantify emissions by itself.

sources.title: Energy efficiency for combustion and energy-from-waste plants
facts: Environment Agency CHP-ready guidance covers BAT energy efficiency for new combustion and energy-from-waste plants.
Assessment considers CHP and carbon-capture readiness.
Design readiness and efficiency potential are not observed GHG emissions.
